NONE: B2 an unusual and mysterious event that is thought to have been caused by a god because it does not follow the usual laws of nature
奇跡
› a very lucky event that is surprising and unexpected
奇事，令人驚歎的事
› an excellent achievement in a particular area of activity
出奇的成就

example: Jesus Christ was said to have performed miracles like turning water into wine.
據說耶穌基督展示了奇跡，例如把水變成葡萄酒。
[ + (that) ] Looking at the state of his car, it's a miracle (that) he wasn't killed!
看看他的車的情況，他沒死真是個奇跡！
I can't promise a miracle cure, but I think we can improve things.
我無法承諾會有奇跡般的解決辦法，但我認為我們可以改善情況。
I considered my recovery to be a miracle of modern medicine.
我認為我的康復是現代醫學的出奇成就。

NONE: › very effective or surprising, or difficult to believe
奇跡般的；令人驚奇的；不可思議的

example: The diet promised miraculous weight loss.
有人保證說按照這個食譜進餐就會有非凡的減肥效果。
Well, you've made a miraculous recovery since last night!
哇，才一個晚上你便奇跡似地康復了！

NONE: › an image, produced by very hot air, of something that seems to be far away but does not really exist
海市蜃樓，蜃景，幻景
› literary a hope or wish that has no chance of being achieved
幻想，妄想

example: Electoral victory is just a distant mirage.
選舉獲勝只是一個可望而不可即的美好幻景。

NONE: › involving warnings that police must give to people they arrest, so that people do not say something that will harm them later in court
（警方放拘捕疑犯時，必須告訴對方有保持沉默的權利，以及對方所說的話可以在法庭上被引用造成不利的）米蘭達警告

example: The Supreme Court's decisions weakened the Miranda rights.
最高法院的判決削弱了米蘭達權利。

C usually singular: › [ C usually singular ] an area of deep, wet, sticky earth

S: › [ S ] literary an unpleasant situation that is difficult to escape

example: We must not be drawn into the mire of civil war.
我們一定不能被拖進內戰的泥潭中。

NONE: › to be involved in a difficult situation, especially for a long period of time
深陷…中

example: The peace talks are mired in bureaucracy.
和平談判深陷於官僚主義的泥潭中。

C: A2 [ C ] a piece of glass with a shiny, metal-covered back that reflects light, producing an image of whatever is in front of it

NONE: › to represent or show something honestly
是…的寫照；是…的真實反映
› to represent something honestly
反映
› to be very similar to something
與…很相似

example: the bathroom mirror
浴室鏡子
She was looking at her reflection in the mirror.
她正看著自己在鏡中的影像。
The movie is a mirror of daily life in wartime Britain.
這部電影真實地反映了英國人在戰時的日常生活。
Our newspaper aims to mirror the opinions of ordinary people.
我們的報紙旨在反映普通民眾的意見。
Her on-screen romances seem to mirror her experiences in her private life.
她在銀幕上的浪漫故事似乎與她的個人經歷很相似。

NONE: › something that looks exactly the same as another thing but with its left and right sides in opposite positions
鏡像，映射
› a person or object that is very similar to another
翻版，相似的人（或物）

example: His home is two terraced houses knocked together, each the mirror image of the other.
他家的房子是兩棟相接的連排房子，兩座房子完全對稱。
The current economic situation is a mirror image of the situation just a few years ago.
目前的經濟形勢完全是幾年前情況的翻版。

NONE: › a website that is an exact copy of another website, but with a different address, allowing more people to be able to see and use it
鏡像網站（與另一個網站除位址以外一切雷同的網站，目的是多吸引使用者）
› with a mirror, or pieces of mirror, on it
帶鏡子的
› laughter, humour, or happiness
歡笑；歡樂，高興

example: Her impersonations of our teachers were a source of considerable mirth.
她對老師的模仿給大家帶來了莫大的歡樂。

NONE: › not showing real enjoyment or happiness
沒有歡樂的；憂鬱的；悲傷的

example: a mirthless laugh/smile
苦笑／面帶悲傷的微笑
